report_name: Oracle Health Breach Exposes Nearly 20 Million Patient Records

threat_actors.name: Unidentified Actor
threat_actors.description: An unidentified threat actor who used compromised customer credentials to access legacy Cerner servers between January and April 2026, leading to the exfiltration of electronic protected health information (ePHI) for nearly 20 million patients.

attack_patterns.name: Valid Accounts
attack_patterns.description: The attacker leveraged compromised customer credentials to access legacy Cerner servers and bypass security controls, operating without triggering alarms associated with brute-force attacks or vulnerability exploitation.

attack_patterns.name: Data from Local System
attack_patterns.description: The attacker collected and exfiltrated a trove of electronic protected health information (ePHI), including names, Social Security numbers, and medical records, from the compromised legacy servers.

identities.name: Oracle Health
identities.description: Parent company of Cerner, whose legacy systems were compromised in the data breach.

identities.name: Cerner
identities.description: The company, now part of Oracle Health, whose legacy systems were targeted and breached using stolen credentials.

identities.name: U.S. Hospitals
identities.description: A class of victims whose patients' data was exposed. The breach affects patients across at least 29 confirmed hospital systems, with reports suggesting the total could be as high as 80.

identities.name: Texas Attorney General's office
identities.description: The government entity that disclosed the vast scope of the data breach.

infrastructure.name: Compromised Cerner Legacy Servers
infrastructure.description: Legacy Cerner servers that had not yet been migrated to Oracle Cloud infrastructure were accessed by the attacker using stolen credentials to exfiltrate patient data.

indicators.name: Anomalous User Login Geolocation
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous User Login Geolocation
id: 2b8c1f9a-7e3d-4b1c-8a9f-0e1d2c3b4a5f
status: experimental
description: Detects user authentications from unusual geographic locations or IP ranges, which could indicate compromised credentials.
references:
  - https://cypro.co.uk/insights/cyber-bulletins/oracle-health-breach-affects-nearly-20-million/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-07
tags:
  - attack.t1078
level: medium
logsource:
  product: azure
  service: signinlogs
detection:
  selection:
    # This is a conceptual rule. A real implementation would require a baseline of normal locations per user.
    # The filter here is an example of known-bad or high-risk locations.
    Location|contains:
      - 'RU'
      - 'CN'
      - 'IR'
      - 'KP'
  filter_known_locations:
    # In a real deployment, this would be a list of expected countries for the user base.
    Location|contains:
      - 'US'
      - 'CA'
      - 'GB'
  condition: selection and not filter_known_locations
indicators.description: Detects user logins from unusual geographic locations or IP ranges, which was suggested as a hunting hint for credential-based attacks.

indicators.name: High Volume Patient Record Access
indicators.pattern:
title: High Volume Patient Record Access
id: 8d9e0f1a-2b3c-4d5e-6f7a-8b9c0d1e2f3a
status: experimental
description: Detects when a single account accesses an unusually high number of patient records, suggesting bulk data exfiltration.
references:
  - https://cypro.co.uk/insights/cyber-bulletins/oracle-health-breach-affects-nearly-20-million/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-07
tags:
  - attack.t1005
level: medium
logsource:
  category: application
  product: generic
detection:
  # This is a conceptual rule. A real implementation would require application-specific fields and UBA capabilities.
  keywords:
    - 'Accessed patient record'
    - 'ePHI view'
  timeframe: 1h
  condition: keywords | count() > 1000 # Threshold is an example
indicators.description: Detects an account accessing an unusually high number of patient records compared to its baseline, a key hunting hint from the report.

indicators.name: Dormant Account Activity
indicators.pattern:
title: Dormant Account Activity
id: 5a6b7c8d-9e0f-4a1b-2c3d-4e5f6a7b8c9d
status: experimental
description: Detects any activity from an account that has been inactive for an extended period, which is highly suspicious.
references:
  - https://cypro.co.uk/insights/cyber-bulletins/oracle-health-breach-affects-nearly-20-million/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-07
tags:
  - attack.t1078
level: high
logsource:
  category: authentication
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    # This rule assumes a mechanism exists to tag or group dormant accounts.
    GroupName|contains: 'Dormant Accounts'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects activity from an account that has been inactive for an extended period, a hunting hint for compromised credentials.
